note.text:
Biologists find out about living things with the scientific approach:
1. Observe and ask a question (Why are the leaves of this plant yellow?).
2. Make a hypothesis: a possible answer that can be tested (It does not get enough light).
3. Plan and do an experiment to test it.
4. Record the results carefully (tables, drawings, measurements).
5. Draw a conclusion: was the hypothesis right?
6. Report what you found so others can check it.
A fair test changes only one thing (the variable) and keeps everything else the same. A control is the set-up that is left unchanged, for comparison. Repeating an experiment makes the results more reliable.

worked_example.problem: Mbah wants to know if bean seeds need water to germinate. He puts seeds on wet cotton in one dish and on dry cotton in another, both in the same warm place. Which dish is the control, and why is it a fair test?
steps: Only one thing is different: water.
The temperature, light and kind of seed are the same.
The dish with wet cotton shows normal conditions to compare with: it is the control.
worked_example.answer: Wet cotton is the control; only the water is changed, so it is fair.

cards.idea: The scientific approach: observe and ask, make a hypothesis, experiment, record, conclude, report.
example: Observation: the leaves are yellow. Hypothesis: the plant lacks light.

cards.idea: A hypothesis is a possible answer that can be tested by an experiment.
example: “Seeds need water to germinate” can be tested.

cards.idea: A fair test changes only one thing and keeps everything else the same; the control is used for comparison.
example: Same seeds, same place, same temperature: only the water changes.

check.prompt: What makes an experiment a fair test?

right.text: Only one thing is changed; everything else stays the same.

wrong.explain: Then you cannot tell which change caused the result.

wrong.text: The experiment is done only once.
wrong.explain: Repeating makes it more reliable, but fairness means changing one thing.
Results must be measured and recorded.
Fairness is about changing only one thing.
